Install t3code on Omarchy

T3 Code is an open-source app that lets you monitor and steer multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok, Antigravity) from a single desktop, web, or mobile interface. It connects to the coding-agent accounts you already pay for rather than reselling usage, and adds features like one-click GitHub pull-request creation with auto-generated titles and diff review.

Watch: So I tried Theo's T3 Code... ↗

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add t3code-bin
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 0.1.0-1:
    pacman -Qi t3code-bin

Open and use t3code

t3code is a desktop app. Press Super + Space to open the launcher and search for it. If it does not show up by name, list the desktop entries the package installed:

pacman -Ql t3code-bin | grep applications

t3code requirements and compatibility

  • Your own credentials/subscription for whichever coding agent(s) you connect (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.)
  • A GitHub account to use the pull-request features

Frequently asked questions

How do I install t3code on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add t3code-bin. The download is 166.1 MB and it takes 453.6 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is t3code free?

Free and open source (no token reselling or quota caps). The package is licensed MIT.

How do I uninstall t3code?

Run omarchy pkg drop t3code-bin. It removes the package from your system.

What does t3code depend on?

The package declares 26 dependencies: alsa-lib, at-spi2-core, cairo, dbus, expat, gcc-libs, glib2, glibc, gtk3, hicolor-icon-theme, libcups, libnotify and more. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is t3code a desktop app?

Yes. Open the launcher with Super + Space and search for t3code.

Is t3code in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as t3code-bin (version 0.1.0-1) in the official Omarchy package repository. Ping.gg makes it. Project site: https://t3.codes. This site is unofficial and not affiliated with Omarchy or Omacom.
